intended_object: The forgetful functor from homological complexes of shape c in V to ι-graded objects in V. It sends a complex to its family of objects (X_i) and a chain map to its family of components, dropping the differentials. Taken from the docstring and the name.
explanation:
The definition is faithful. On objects it sends C to C.X : ι → V, which is the family of objects of the complex. On morphisms it sends f to f.f, which is the family of components of the chain map. That is exactly the functor that forgets the differential. Because composition and identities of chain maps are defined componentwise, the functor laws hold automatically.

It is stated in full generality: for any category V with zero morphisms (needed for HomologicalComplex to make sense at all) and any complex shape c on any index type ι. This file is the place where Mathlib itself defines the notion, so there is no other Mathlib declaration to cite.
